newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Firm resources support Australia stocks at close.
newsitem.headline: Firm resources support Australia stocks at close.

text.p: SPI Sycom cl 2526.0 -13.0 US 30yr cl 6.92 +0.01

*Buoyant resources offset weak banks to drag overall stocks to steady close after early softness. Volume 324.08 million, value A$874.08 million, 1,076 stocks traded, 351 steady, 320 up, 405 down.
Australian stocks ended barely changed on Tuesday with all eyes on the U.S. as traders waited to assess any rate implications of the FOMC meeting later today.

The All Ordinaries Index shed a wafer-thin 0.3 points to 2,530.7. The June Share Price Index futures contract was down 13 points at 2,526, a 4.7 point discount to the underlying index as traders took a cautious stance ahead of possible U.S. gyrations.

Local trade was just more of the same seen in the last few days, with the favoured key miners battling it out with a bank-weakened industrial grouping to produce the stalemate that was the day's finish.
Bellwether and copper major Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and diversified miner RTZ-CRA led the fight for the resources, both adding over one percent to A$19.26 and A$21.12 respectively.
"Without those two doing what they did, the statistics would be a lot worse," said broker Helen Michael, of Melbourne-based firm Peake Lands Kirwan.
Other resource majors were not so lucky, with energy group Woodside Petroleum sliding two percent to A$10.94 after oil prices slipped offshore and as recent talk of potential takeovers evaporated.
"There was a fair bit of anticipation and when it did not come about, people may have taken some profits," Michael said.

Topping turnover was Austrim Ltd with 26.98 million shares traded, the bulk of it in a line of 13.18 million shares specialled twice at A$2.80 a share. The 9.2 percent stake is exactly equal to that owned by a private company associated with Seven Network Chairman Kerry Stokes. Austrim shares ended nine cents higher at A$2.89.
Food group Burns Philp & Co lost nine cents to A$1.87 amid concerns about its decision to sell more promising assets after Monday's restructuring announcement.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was lighter than recent days as traders awaited the results of the FOMC meeting. Options trade was also slower.
Total options traded 32,698 (36,754)
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 4,606 (6,220)

In other local markets, Australian bonds notched up a very quiet day as the market bided its time ahead of the FOMC meeting and two pieces of local wages data later this week. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were steady at 7.66 percent.

The Australian dollar clung tightly to its U.S. counterpart as both were buried beneath a torrent of distressed selling against the yen. By 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.7743/48. ----------------------(TECHNICALS)----------------------------
